title: Make bee state file writes survive a crash
action: In fsutil.rs, write_json_atomic and write_text_atomic must flush the tmp file's data to disk (File::sync_all) before the rename, and after a successful rename sync the parent directory so the new name is durable. append_jsonl must sync the appended data (sync_data) before it returns. Directory sync is Unix-only: on Windows skip it (opening a directory as a File fails there), gated with cfg(unix). Keep every public signature, the tmp-name scheme, the tmp cleanup on error, and the exact bytes written. A parent-directory sync failure after a successful rename returns the error to the caller (the file is already in place; the error must say the rename landed). Add unit tests in fsutil's test module: the written bytes are unchanged for both atomic writers and append_jsonl, no tmp file is left beside the target after success, and the tmp is removed when the rename fails. Measure the declared suite's wall time before and after and record both numbers in the cap proof; if the suite slows by more than 15%, stop and report instead of capping.

truths: write_json_atomic and write_text_atomic call sync_all on the tmp file before rename
the parent directory is synced after rename on unix
bytes on disk are identical to before the change
